clue.text: The odd male ran, and then he appeared early

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters that follow are put into an unusual order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A strange man runs off, and then turns up ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odd male' looks like the subject of the sentence, but 'The odd' is the anagram signal and only 'male ran, and then' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This prehistoric human species lived tens of thousands of years ago, so he appeared early in human history.

clue.text: State assets

parts.note: surface reading: property held by one of the states of a federation
setter's reading: the total resources owned by a nation

explanation.walkthrough: A plain definition: 'State' means a country as a whole rather than one state of a federation.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's combined resources and property make up its riches, the assets of the state.

clue.text: Possibly unite as members of a family

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Relatives may come together as one family.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunties are a parent's sisters, so they are relatives within a family.

clue.text: Application for a coach

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a public stagecoach in France and elsewhere in Europe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Application for a coach' sounds like a job form for a sports trainer; 'coach' is the horse-drawn kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence means persistent careful work, and was also the name of the old French stagecoach.

clue.text: Scatter as the result of a tirade

indicators.note: the result of something is what it turns into, so the following letters turn into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People flee in all directions after someone's angry rant.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to spread out from a centre in all directions, which is what scattering does.

clue.text: They'll lift great weights, the man maintains

parts.note: he refers to a man
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: A man insists that these people can lift enormous loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintains' looks like it means holds up, but it means asserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A heaver is someone who heaves, hauling up heavy loads, so heavers lift great weights.

clue.text: The landowner is placed about right.

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for placed surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: laid means placed down
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The owner of the estate is set right beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is the Scots word for a landowner, the sort of term worth knowing for Scottish-flavoured clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish term for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: A place of learning made changes in one

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for one
changes means altered, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of made, rearranged
an ace is a one on a card or die

explanation.surface: One school or college brought in reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a single place, but it is the card name for one, which opens up to hold the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world or a university, from Plato's Academy, a place where learning goes on.

clue.text: Characteristic of those who are not dextrous

definitions.text: Characteristic of those who are not dextrous

parts.note: surface reading: clumsy, lacking skill with the hands
setter's reading: dexter is Latin for right, so these people do not favour the right hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dextrous' looks like it means skilful, but it is read through its root, Latin dexter, right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring the left hand is the trait of people who do not use the right hand by preference.

clue.text: Coloured outside left caused a thrill

indicators.note: outside says the colour word goes around the letter for left, enclosing it

parts.note: tinged means slightly coloured
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something coloured on the left wing caused excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' reads as a football position, but it is an instruction to place L inside TINGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tingle is to feel a prickling thrill, so something that tingled gave or felt a thrill.

clue.text: Trouble — a barrier is required to contain it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to contain means the barrier wraps around the following word, holding it inside

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem needs a fence or wall to keep it in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun for the trouble, but it is taken literally as two letters held inside the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or upset, a verb synonym of trouble as in 'troubled by the news'.

clue.text: Due to fly round first

indicators.note: first says the round shape is placed at the front, ahead of the word for fly, despite the clue order

parts.note: O is a round shape
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Something is scheduled to circle before anything else happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the round letter comes before the word for fly, even though fly is read first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owing is due to be paid; both describe money not yet settled.

clue.text: Met men and maybe called for some improvement

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting of men demanded that things be made better.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to put something right, such as a correction to a law or document.

clue.text: Dope gets in, they agree

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
enters means gets in

explanation.surface: A drug gets smuggled through, and everyone is fine with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Assenters are people who assent, that is, who give their agreement to something.

clue.text: Statue presented by two Greek characters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A statue offered to the city by a pair of Greek benefactors.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letter names are joined, PI first, then ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pietà is a sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, most famously Michelangelo's in St Peter's.

clue.text: A course set at intervals?

parts.note: surface reading: a course of study or a race laid out in stages
setter's reading: a meal course, done bit by bit with gaps between

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into piece and meal, and a meal is served in courses; the whole word means done a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal describes something done gradually in separate stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: A little note that's not at all colourful

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a minim or semibreve, drawn as an open head

explanation.surface: A brief memo written in a dull, uncoloured style.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the loosest part: open-headed notes such as the minim are called white notes in music.
explanation.definitionFit: White is commonly called the absence of colour, so it fits something with no colour at all.

clue.text: Stonily do the decorating

parts.note: surface reading: someone paints the house with a stony expression
setter's reading: to decorate with a covering layer of stones or gems

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stonily' reads as describing the decorator's mood, but it says how the decorating is done: with stones set into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To incrust, more often spelt encrust, is to ornament a surface by covering it with a layer of jewels or stones.

clue.text: The theatre-worker needs gas — and the alternative

indicators.note: an alternative is a different version, so the letters before it take a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the dash

explanation.surface: A worker in the theatre wants gas lighting, or else some other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The alternative' reads as 'or something else', but 'the' belongs to the fodder and 'alternative' alone asks for a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves scenery and props behind the scenes, so is a backstage employee in a theatre.

clue.text: Mounting a single Lily, like some Japanese

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting means climbing upwards, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an arum is a kind of lily
as means like

explanation.surface: Climbing up to a lone lily, as some Japanese gardeners do.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, so some Japanese people.

clue.text: Increasing by about fifty is so confusing

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for increasing by wraps around the numeral

parts.note: adding means increasing by an amount
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Raising something by about fifty makes it very hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About fifty' looks like an approximate figure, but 'about' places L inside ADDING.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or confuse, so addling means making confused.

clue.text: The language of a university man held by soldiers in charge!

indicators.note: held by means placed inside, so the graduate's letters sit within the soldiers and the charge abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
RA is the Royal Artillery
an MA is a Master of Arts, a university graduate
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A graduate held captive by soldiers speaks a strange tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the usual crossword soldiers; the graduate sits inside soldiers-plus-charge, with the opening A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language, spoken in biblical times across the Near East.

clue.text: Cheered as a number made demands

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to claim is to demand as a right

explanation.surface: People cheered while a crowd made their demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a crowd, but it supplies A and the Roman numeral C.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to applaud or hail with enthusiasm, a synonym of cheered.

clue.text: A regressive attitude for a writer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for attitude is written from its end

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A backward-looking outlook is no help to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word for attitude is reversed; the A stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author to whom the famous animal fables are credited.

clue.text: Aim to include the French beast

indicators.note: to include means the word for aim goes around the French article, holding it

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
la is the feminine French for the

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to bring the French into contact with an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' points to the French word for 'the', here its feminine form.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, so it is a kind of animal or beast.

clue.text: He's bound to be more precise about a certain craft

definitions.note: loose: a trusser is one who binds, not one who is bound

indicators.note: about means the comparative word goes around the vessel abbreviation, surrounding it

parts.note: truer means more accurate
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a particular kind of vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor is sure to be more exact about how his boat is handled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the weakest link: a trusser binds things up, so 'He's bound' must be read loosely as the man connected with binding.
explanation.definitionFit: To truss is to tie up tightly, as with a chicken before roasting, so a trusser is a person who ties.

clue.text: Repeat of a trite broadcast by egg head

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: only the opening letter of egg is kept

explanation.surface: An intellectual delivers a rerun of some tired old programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg head' looks like egghead, an intellectual, but it means only the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, a direct synonym of the verb repeat.

clue.text: Traffic halts which may have a bearing on capital deposits

parts.note: surface reading: spots on a route where vehicles pull up

parts.words: which may have a bearing on capital deposits
parts.note: setter's reading: these are where passengers get off, deposited in a capital city

explanation.surface: Traffic stops that might affect money held in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful gloss rather than wordplay: 'capital deposits' suggests money in a bank, but buses and trains deposit people at such spots in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where vehicles stop on a route, such as bus stops, are where traffic halts.
